Dončić and the 11-2, West-leading Lakers have been a buzzsaw offensively this season. Generating 122.5 points per 100 possessions, they own the NBA's top-ranked offense, per Cleaning the Glass. Dončić himself is averaging a preposterous 38.6 points and 7.6 assists per game while shooting 58.7% inside the arc and a career-high 40.8% from deep. He's taking a league-high 13.4 triples each night and making a league-high 5.5 of them. The Lakers are scoring 131.0 points per 100 possessions when he's on the court.

Dončić may be the engine but his backcourt buddy, Reaves, is crucial to Los Angeles' success and also off to a ripping start. He's averaging 24.7 points and 4.7 assists on a .513/.409/.915 shooting split. If those marks hold, he'd join the prestigious 50-40-90 club, which currently features nine NBA players, five of whom are MVPs and eight of whom are All-NBA honorees.

#2758. John Harbaugh knew about the Jameis Winston "who let the dogs out?" cadence

Thursday night’s game between the Commanders and the Giants introduced a new wrinkle to the legend of Jameis Winston.

While attempting to get the Washington defense to jump offside on a fourth-and-one play in the fourth quarter, Jameis capped his pre-snap call with, “Who let the dogs out?”

The move invited curiosity as to whether Jameis was simply being Jameis and seizing on the moment, or whether coach John Harbaugh knew that the homage to the Baha Men was part of the plan.

Last night, it’s possible that the specific cadence could have prompted one of the defenders to start laughing loud enough to tumble forward in his stance.

Regardless, it was fun. And that’s when football is at its best — when it’s fun.

#2751. He’s here, he’s there, he’s every-f—ing-where, VJ Edgecombe

Ted Lasso became an iconic show in short order.

The Jason Sudeikis-led comedy series about an American football coach who becomes a football (soccer) coach became a cultural phenomenon.

One of the most popular characters is Roy Kent, the grizzled old veteran of A.F.C. Richmond. Kent, portrayed by writer and comedian Brett Goldstein, was once a star of the Premier League, but he's on his last legs when we meet him in the show.

Fans of Kent made up a song at his peak, one they serenaded him with as he gets hurt and leaves the pitch for the final time.

He's here, he's there, he's every-fucking-where, Roy Kent, Roy Kent

Though he's only in his second year — and is the polar opposite of "grizzled" — VJ Edgecombe has embodied that song in his young NBA career. There was no clearer example of that than his performance in the Sixers' 123-112 win over the Toronto Raptors Thursday night.

With LeBron James out of the lineup, Edgecombe stepped into a bigger role and looked comfortable in it.

"I'm blessed to have a group of guys around me that's encouraging," Edgecombe said postgame. "They help me with confidence."

Edgecombe scored 15 points with multiple dazzling finishes at the rim, a couple serious dunks (and then teasing the possibility of doing the dunk contest postgame) and a three. He drove to the rim and made the right reads all night, finding his teammates for eight assists. He continued to crash the glass at a high level for a guard, pulling down eight rebounds. He also continued to defend at a high level, recording three steals and a block.

All of this and the general winning plays he makes on a nightly basis have become what's expected of him.

"I just tell him to go do that VJ stuff," Tyrese Maxey said. "Literally, that's exactly what I tell him. I say, 'Hey, man, go do that VJ stuff that you do,' and he literally goes out there and does VJ stuff. He had 15, eight and eight tonight. Who knows? Next game it may be 20, four and four. He just does VJ stuff. He gets us loose balls. He makes winning plays. He defends. He scores. He does it all."

So much of the noise this offseason surrounding the super team of James, Maxey, Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown the Sixers have built was about Edgecombe. How would he handle his role changing? Would a drop in usage affect his development? Would the glut of stars hurt Edgecombe's chances to put up numbers and earn his eventual rookie max extension?

Nights like Thursday show why those queries were silly.

"When I'm on the floor with those four other guys, it's kind of in a way where it's helpful for me," Edgecombe said, "because I'm in different positions and I'm in a year two — I'm seeing basketball from different standpoints. Some nights two of them might be out. Some nights one might be out. Some nights none might be out. And to be able to just balance the different lineups and just trying to stay consistent throughout it all.

"I just want to shout out my teammates for that. They just helped me a lot, especially 'Rese and Joel. They always just tell me keep going, keep going."

Anyone who watched Edgecombe as a rookie and heard him talk knew he'd excel with this star-studded group. Last season, Edgecombe's usage was unexpectedly high because the Sixers needed it to be. This season, they've needed Edgecombe to flash more of his overall game.

And 13 games in, that's exactly what he's done.

But when guys are out of the lineup, Edgecombe knows his team needs more.

"I think this is like the second time he's done this as well when we're down somebody that he just comes out a little bit more lively and assertive," Nick Nurse said. "And I thought … he made some really decisive moves in the open floor — not necessarily break situations, but the flow is still going, and he's punching through.

"And again, I thought he kicked out a few of those, and even on some of the half-court sets, he just attacked aggressively to the paint, and that's where some of those assists were coming from. So, I just thought he did come with an extra pop, and he's done that a couple times now this year."

When Edgecombe was coming out of Baylor, there were comparisons to old friend Jimmy Butler. This writer didn't see it at the time, but now it makes sense.

Some players simply impact winning. They affect the game in every facet. They stuff the stat sheet, but their imprint on the game goes far beyond it.

He's here, he's there, he's every-fucking-where. VJ, Edgecombe

"I'm just blessed to be in this position," Edgecombe said, "and at the end of the day, I just want to keep getting better. Some opportunities might not be there, but I think I'm getting better mentally, and that's the most important part of the game. Sometimes you got to be mentally strong."

#2748. JJ Redick Provides Key Updates On Injured Lakers Days Before Suns Game

The Los Angeles Lakers (11-2) currently lead the Western Conference standings, but they face multiple injuries ahead of Sunday's game against the Phoenix Suns (5-6). Fortunately, they've avoided any long-term setbacks, but Lakers fans are still concerned about the team's current state.

That's why, on Friday, head coach JJ Redick provided clarity in a chat with the media, revealing the latest development with each of the four injured Lakers guards: Austin Reaves, Luka Doncic, Collin Sexton, and Quentin Grimes.

"Luka is fine," said Redick on Friday, via Mark Medina. "The expectation would be that he's available. AR is based on his physical evaluation and how he was feeling yesterday. We opted against imaging; he'll be day-to-day. We'll have him on the report tomorrow at 5:00. Collin is in the same boat. Concussion's been ruled out; he ended up getting stitches, and he'll be day-to-day. And then Q [Quentin Grimes] was able to do the live part of the stay-ready game."

Plenty of NBA teams have been plagued by injuries this season, and the Lakers are no exception. Since opening night, they've had various players in and out of the lineup, but it hasn't made much of a difference. Thanks to Redick's coaching, a loaded roster, and heroics from Luka (averaging 38.6 points, 7.5 rebounds, 7.6 assists, 2.0 steals, and 0.7 blocks per game on 48.9% shooting), they've been a dominant force in the West, but things could always take a turn for the worse.

In that one game against the Milwaukee Bucks on November 11th, four different players got banged up, including Doncic himself. The MVP frontrunner turned his ankle late in the fourth quarter on Wednesday, raising fears he could miss time. Fortunately, he woke up pain-free the following morning, all but sealing his active status for Sunday's game.

It's a similar story with guard Quentin Grimes, who has provided a major boost off the bench with averages of 8.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 0.9 steals, and 0.2 blocks per game on 43.1% shooting from the field. With a sprained finger, his condition was never serious, and Redick confirmed today that he was well enough to participate in live contact drills.

6'5″ guard Austin Reaves is facing a slightly more serious situation. He only played 25 minutes against the Bucks after landing awkwardly on a dunk in the third quarter. He tested negative for an Achilles injury and opted out of further tests as he works toward a quick return. He's currently day-to-day, suggesting that he might need more time to get his body right. This season, in 12 games, he's averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists, 1.2 steals, and 0.3 blocks per game on 51.3% shooting from the field.

For Collin Sexton, concussion protocol was activated after a head-to-head collision with Ryan Rollins. He needed stitches to fix a cut above his right eye, but the Lakers confirmed that he suffered no other complications. He should be cleared to play on Sunday, but there's still a chance he could sit if the Lakers prefer to be extra cautious.

With the rest of today and all of tomorrow to rest and heal, the Lakers are likely at full strength for their next game, and we know what that means for their chances of victory. What's better, with showdowns against the Hornets, Jazz, and Kings on their schedule, this next stretch of games could easily extend their win streak.

Brown’s best year came in 2021, with 91 catches for 1,008 yards and six touchdowns.

#2738. Grading the Mavericks: Cooper Flagg is awesome, and he is only going to get better

The Mavericks went 3-1 over the last week and sit at 7-5 overall. They won three in a row at home against Utah (112-100), Brooklyn (130-93), and Indiana (125-122). Minnesota pummeled them to start off their road trip, 133-94. Cooper Flagg led the team in scoring with 25.3 points per game.

The Mavericks, once again, had a three-game win streak spoiled by an embarrassing loss. The Timberwolves are much better than the Kings, but the effort from Dallas was similar. Minnesota got any shot they wanted, exposed the Mavericks' size and lack of point-of-attack defenders, and effectively ended the game in the second quarter.

The three games prior, however, were great. The Mavericks took care of business against two bad teams and beat an Indiana team that always gives them problems. Morez Johnson Jr. has been awesome in his minutes; his early-season coup de grace was a 13-point, 17-rebound (10 offensive) performance against Utah, where he truly looked like the ninth pick for the first time. He said after the game that he was "back", implying that the injury that hindered him to start the year had dissipated.

Caleb Martin has been good in his role as defensive connector. P.J. Washington's jump shot looks so much better this season, likely because he is using his legs more. Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving's chemistry continues to develop as Irving gets healthier. Speaking of which, Irving played his first back-to-back of the season against Brooklyn and Indiana. Zaccharie Risacher has had his minutes go up and down, mostly correlated to how he is playing game to game. Naji Marshall is one piece that still has not felt right on this team, and his trade status will need to be monitored going forward.

The Mavericks have to wash the stink of the Timberwolves loss as they head to Cleveland and Boston on a Saturday/Sunday back-to-back, and then back home for Golden State on Wednesday.

Let's ignore Flagg's stinker against Minnesota for a second. In the three-game win streak prior, he averaged 29.7 points, 8.3 rebounds, 8.3 assists, shot seven-of-15 from three, and had nine stocks (steals plus blocks). This included a 43-point, 10-rebound game, which brings his 40-point game total as a teenager to five, the most all-time. He also sits only behind LeBron James in 25-point, 5-rebound, 5-assist games as a teenager (Flagg 17, James 22), with 13 games scheduled plus the NBA Cup before his 20th birthday,

He is awesome. He is a joy to watch, a fierce competitor, and improves (almost) every game. When his three-point shot is on, as it was over the last four games, he is truly unguardable at age 19. Of course, the preface to this section was ignoring his poor performance in Minnesota. He still has weird off-nights. But he is not even 20 years old, and those should phase out as he grows. One thing has been clear in 12 games so far: a team Cooper Flagg will not be able to lose very often.

Gafford has largely been good this year. He has been healthy, which is key, and he certainly is a lob threat on offense. But his weaknesses, particularly on defense, have been exposed recently. He cannot move in space effectively, which forces him to play drop coverage on pick-and-rolls. This means he drops back in the paint to guard the screener, which inherently leaves space for the ball handler to shoot or pass. Teams have been exploiting this, and it even got him benched against the Jazz.

His shot-blocking and big dunks are cool to watch, don't get me wrong. But Gafford has a bit of the "Boban Syndrome", where he is really good in short spurts and really bad when he plays extended periods. His minutes in the last four games are already down to just 18.3 a game, eclipsed by Morez Johnson Jr.'s 18.8. With Gafford, less is more. Unfortunately, this means they need their rookie undersized center, who is fresh off shin splints, will need to play more. Dallas may survive, but against bigger teams like the Timberwolves, they're going to struggle mightily.

Clayton Jr. has been one of the more underrated signings in the entirety of the NBA this season. His stats do not jump off the page (7.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.5 assists per game), but when you watch him play, he looks like he belongs. This Dallas roster was in dire need of guard play, and Clayton Jr., last year's 18th overall pick, has given them great minutes at the one.

His assists come with just 1.6 turnovers per game, and he is shooting 37.1 percent from three. His hands on defense are active, which really stands out because he gets a lot of deflections. He is under control handling the ball, and already has the trust of the coaching staff to finish games. Normally, individual plus/minus is a flawed stat because there are four other guys on the court. However, Clayton Jr.'s +43 when he is on the floor this season backs up the eye test. He looks like an NBA point guard, and if he can keep this up, this would be Masai Ujiri's crown jewel early in his tenure.

#2735. France hold nerve to edge past South Africa in thriller

Tries: Grandidier-Nkanang, Attissogbe, Bielle-Biarrey Cons: Lucu (3)

Tries: Wessels, Reinach, Marx Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu (2)

France held on to end their five-match losing run against South Africa at Stade de France with an enthralling 21-19 victory in Paris.

The victory dents the world champions' hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final and puts Les Bleus in a strong position to top the northern hemisphere standings.

The hosts, inspired by their captain Antoine Dupont, showed their class and skill to score three first-half tries.

France's back three of Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey all crossed in a thrilling opening 40 minutes.

The Springboks' try came before Bielle-Biarrey's, with Jan-Hendrik Wessels scoring off the back of a maul.

Number eight Jasper Wiese was shown a 20-minute red card early in the second half for a tucked-shoulder charge, but it had the opposite effect to derailing the world champions.

Replacement scrum-half Cobus Reinach and hooker Malcolm Marx scored to set a thrilling finale, with South Africa's set-piece power proving too much.

However, Manie Libbok missed the vital conversion to Marx's try that would have levelled the game.

With South Africa pushing for a winning score, Bielle-Biarrey produced a huge defensive play to force the ball loose, before Dupont, who was named player of the match, gathered possession to help seal the victory.

The result will come as a blow to both England and Ireland, who are in direct competition with France for a place in the Nations Championship final at the end of the month.

Les Bleus, who are six points clear at the top of the northern hemisphere standings, now face Argentina next Saturday, putting them in a strong position to reach the final at Allianz Stadium on Sunday, 29 November.

Injuries to France's three first-choice fly-halves - Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack and Antoine Hastoy - left France coach Fabien Galthie with little option but to deploy his captain and talismanic scrum-half at number 10.

Despite wearing the France number 10 shirt for the first time, Dupont lined up at scrum-half, as Galthie played Erasmus, who had again swapped his entire front row an hour before kick-off, at his own game.

It was an electric start from the hosts, as a clever move sent Kalvin Gourgues through a gap, with Grandidier-Nkanang eventually crossing in the corner.

A monstrous left-footed 50:22 from Dupont, with South Africa lock Lood de Jager in the sin-bin for a high tackle, gave France the field position, before the ball cannoned off Gourgues' head and Attissogbe crossed for a fortunate try.

Dupont supplied more magic, grubber kicking through on his stronger right foot for Bielle-Biarrey to score.

South Africa's power told as they scored their opening try from a maul, before Erasmus changed his entire front row again, five minutes before half-time.

Dupont did slot in at fly-half but mainly was deployed in his familiar position of scrum-half [Getty Images]

Creativity, intensity and physicality - it was a first game that felt remarkably similar to the epic quarter-final of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in Paris.

Despite losing Wiese to a 20-minute red card early in the second half, the world champions took advantage of Grandidier-Nkanang's sin-bin for a deliberate knock-on.

Tiredness and poor discipline made the game loose and chaotic, before the Springboks turned to their scrum to regain control.

A succession of scrum penalties resulted in another sin-bin, with replacement France prop Regis Montagne yellow carded as the hosts were left clinging on for the final 10 minutes.

Stunning scramble defence and sheer grit showed a side to the back-to-back Six Nations champions France that has often been questioned.

Despite their scrum crumbling, France held firm, continuing to chase kicks and compete for loose balls.

A draw would have felt a fair result given the contrasting nature of the two halves, but Libbok - as at the 2023 World Cup - badly shanked a kick that will once again raise questions over his ability to deliver under pressure in the biggest Test matches.

For once, the fine margins went against South Africa, who won every knockout game of the last World Cup by a point.

They face Ireland in Dublin next Saturday and will now likely need a favour from England, who take on New Zealand earlier that same day, if they are to reclaim top spot in the southern hemisphere standings.

#2732. LaMelo Ball sure looks like the difference: Timberwolves and Hornets trending in opposite directions after trade

We will stipulate that, when it comes to success and struggle in the NBA, the answer is never just one thing. There's plenty that goes into teams' fortunes rising and falling, and all sorts of stuff can factor into the difference between living in the penthouse and taking up residence in the outhouse.

With that caveat in place: While the Minnesota Timberwolves were doing this in Minneapolis on Thursday, en route to dismantling the Dallas Mavericks, 133-94 …

… and the Charlotte Hornets were doing this in Phoenix on the same night, en route to a desultory 101-96 defeat …

… it was hard not to note the Just One Thing that seems to be contributing to the difference between Minnesota and Charlotte. Or, rather, the Guy Wearing No. 1.

After walloping a pretty good Mavs team, the Wolves are 9-3, in third place in the Western Conference, with the NBA's best net rating. They've won five in a row, and six out of eight since losing superstar No. 1 option Anthony Edwards to knee surgery. They've outscored their opponents by a total of 161 points this season; according to Justin Kubatko of Statitudes, that's the largest point differential through 12 games in Wolves franchise history — by 50 points.

After falling in Phoenix, mustering just 96 points against the league's fourth-worst defense, the Hornets are now 4-8, tied for 10th in the East, with the NBA's No. 26 net rating. They've lost seven of eight, have logged more turnovers than assists four times in 12 games, and have already failed to crack 100 points six times — as many times as Charlotte finished south of the century mark all of last season.

Again: It's not just that LaMelo Ball used to play for the Hornets, and now he plays for the Wolves. The operating theory for how Charlotte would generate offense in the absence of its one-time linchpin rested largely on continued growth and elevated production from Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel and the re-signed Coby White, with a dash of second-unit contribution from veteran Dennis Schröder. The Hornets have gotten a grand total of 97 minutes thus far from White, who's on a minutes restriction as he works his way back from a left calf strain, and Knueppel, who'll miss the next several weeks with a balky left hamstring. Schröder's also on the shelf with a hamstring strain; Miller, the team's leading scorer, has missed the last two games with a groin injury.

Any team would struggle to score without the bulk of its perimeter firepower, ball-handling and shot creation. It has to be painful, though, to be mired in such a horrific offensive morass mere months after consciously choosing to bid farewell to Ball, the player whom both the eye test and the advanced numbers suggested served as the rising tide that lifted Charlotte's offense last season.

And it must be particularly galling to be suffering through the doldrums while watching LaMelo have exactly the same kind of effusive, elevating effect in the Twin Cities.

Ball had nine of the Wolves' 33 assists in the blowout win over the Mavericks on Thursday — Minnesota's fourth 30-assist game of the season, more than anybody but the Hawks, Warriors, Nuggets and Spurs. Those helpers led to 19 Minnesota points, in addition to the 22 that Ball scored himself; for the season, he's directly creating 56.9 points of offense per 100 possessions for the Wolves, according to Databallr, which is 20th in the NBA — and nearly five points-per-100 more than White, who leads this season's Hornets.

The Wolves generate a higher share of their shots at the rim when LaMelo's on the floor than when he's off it. Their 3-point shooting goes through the roof in his minutes, and nearly every member of the team sees a bump in shot quality when playing alongside him.

The Wolves are more efficient in the half-court when Ball's at the controls, and they get out in transition way more often with him out there. Minnesota's team-wide effective field-goal percentage spikes by 6.5% with LaMelo on the floor — the largest on/off split on the team, and one of the largest among all NBA players to log at least 200 minutes this season, according to Cleaning the Glass.

The numbers tell a compelling story. So, too, does the joy that seems to leap off the screen from so many of the Wolves as they run with LaMelo — orbiting, emulating and ultimately benefiting from the irrepressible style and flow with which he plays.

"I think when you have a guy like Melo, he makes it fun for everybody," Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch said after Thursday's win, according to Sarah Todd of the Minnesota Star Tribune. "And the guys can trust in the next pass, next play."

That trust is tougher to come by these days in Charlotte, where the Hornets enter Friday's action ranked dead last in the NBA in points scored per possession, field-goal percentage, free-throw attempts, assists and turnovers, struggling to consistently string together quality possessions, even against lesser defensive outfits.

"How do we stop the bleeding?" White told reporters after a recent loss to the Detroit Pistons. "There's gonna be turnovers. There's gonna be miscommunications on both sides of the ball. How do we not let it continue to derail us from what we're trying to do?"

The loss of a superstar of Edwards' magnitude would've derailed plenty of teams. The Wolves, though, have continued to thrive, buoyed in part by the NBA's No. 1 defense — a unit on which Ball has somewhat surprisingly emerged as a physical and positive contributor at the point of attack. All told, Minnesota has outscored opponents by a whopping 15.5 points per 100 possessions when Ball has played without Edwards — a loftier net rating than even their regular-season leading mark, and more than good enough to stay afloat in the brutally competitive West while Ant continues to rehab his ailing knee.

There are plenty of other factors at play. The Hornets have underperformed their expected shot quality by more than any other team in the NBA thus far, according to Synergy Sports Technology's tracking; the combination of some regression to the mean and the hopefully healthy return of some key pieces should help bolster their offense. And there's plenty of credit to go around in Minnesota, from Rudy Gobert's perpetually stalwart work on the back line to Finch getting career-best play from the likes of Jonathan Kuminga, Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland to a collective closing kick that has the Wolves ranked second in the NBA in fourth-quarter net rating.

"We've definitely [elevated] our play in the fourth quarters on both sides of the ball," Finch said. "Getting key stops, rebounding really well, executing, finding really good shots. And LaMelo's been at the heart of a lot of that on offense."

LaMelo's presence has been at the heart of a lot of what's gone well for the Wolves, and his absence, it seems, has been at the heart of a lot of what's haunting the Hornets. It's never just one thing. Sometimes, though, one thing can make one hell of a big difference.

#2720. Erik Van Rooyen Says LIV Stars Must Re-Qualify

Erik Van Rooyen said on Thursday that players who left for LIV Golf cannot simply walk back onto the PGA Tour. The South African golfer insists that former members must earn their spots through the standard qualifying process. During the Austin Championship, he started with a 64 that had no bogeys when he made those comments. While his ball-striking drew attention, his stance on tour rules sparked a bigger debate about fairness.

Van Rooyen believes the path back depends entirely on a player's current status. "I think it's completely status dependent, right? Like Jon Rahm has no reason to go back to Q-School," van Rooyen said Thursday. He argues that top stars might have other ways to return, but the rest must pay their dues. This view opposes the idea of a quick fix for the sport.

The 36-year-old pointed to his own career struggles to make his case. He started the 2026 season with nine straight missed cuts before finding his form again. Van Rooyen noted that if he had left for a different tour, he would lose his privileges. Returning would require him to work his way back up. "I have nothing against players that went to LIV, nothing personal at all," van Rooyen said. "But that's just how things work, right? So shouldn't we just follow the rules?"

This demand places him against those who want a fast track for ex-LIV players. The PGA Tour faces a tough choice as the rival league collapses. Some stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Tyrrell Hatton might need to rebuild their status from scratch. Van Rooyen's position ensures that the field remains competitive for everyone who stayed loyal.

The conversation extends beyond the United States. Peter Baker, a three-time European Tour winner, wants the DP World Tour to stop sending ten players to the PGA Tour every year. Baker told Golf Monthly that the current setup is flawed. "I certainly wouldn't be sending 10 of our best players over to America every year to play there, I think that needs to be looked at," he said, according to Yahoo. He believes the European circuit should be its own strong entity again.

Baker admitted the DP World Tour has struggled since LIV arrived. "It has been in a tricky spot for a while I think with LIV," he said. However, he sees a chance for the tour to grow now that the Saudi-backed league is fading. He wants the best players to stay home and support the European schedule rather than chasing money in America.

Van Rooyen is advocating changes to entry rules, while 91‑year‑old Gary Player is advocating the game itself. The Golfer's Journal was informed by Player that the golf ball needs an immediate rollback. He warned that modern power is destroying course design. "The game is changing against my better wishes," Player said, according to Yahoo Sports. He claims pros now hit drivers and eight-irons into par-5s, making old courses obsolete.

Player predicts the problem will get worse before it gets better. He stated, "Wait until the Michael Jordans and Shaq O'Neals come out and play golf. We haven't scratched the surface." He estimates that at least a trillion dollars is being wasted globally on course modifications to handle longer drives. The delay in implementing a ball rollback until 2030 has frustrated traditionalists who want immediate action.

Van Rooyen's stance on Q-School remains clear as the Austin Championship continues. He wants the standards to apply fairly to everyone, regardless of where they played last year.

#2717. Pelicans evaluating possibilities after trade request from Dejounte Murray, who recently rebutted criticism on social media

The New Orleans Pelicans are evaluating potential trade opportunities for Dejounte Murray after a trade request from the All-Star guard, the team announced Friday.

The news comes the same week the 30-year-old Murray rebutted criticism on social media with since-deleted posts, one of which reportedly featured profanity. The Pelicans are 4-8 this season, including 1-8 in the games Murray has appeared in.

Murray won't play in Friday night's NBA Cup group-play game between New Orleans and the Memphis Grizzlies, the Pelicans announced, citing his left ankle sprain. His agent Rich Paul and Pelicans officials were reported by ESPN's Shams Charania to be working on a resolution earlier in the day.

The Phoenix Suns have expressed interest in the 2022 All-Star, according to NBA insider Chris Haynes.

The 2026-27 campaign is his third with the Pelicans, with whom he's currently averaging 13.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.6 steals per game.

That said, Murray is shooting just 29.6% from 3, and he's committed four turnovers twice so far.

In the fallout of a 145-111 home loss to the 3-8 Brooklyn Nets, the X account for Pro Pels Talk, a Pelicans podcast, posted an array of game clips, breaking down the game film without mincing words. The commentary that accompanied some of those clips questioned Murray's on-court effort.

As reported by The Athletic, Murray responded to one of those posts, which showcased footage of him apparently misplacing a pass intended for forward Saddiq Bey. The ball ended up low and away, resulting in a turnover, whereas Bey seemed to be asking for it near chest level.

"Ohhhhh let's talk about it," Murray wrote back on X in a since-deleted post, per The Athletic. "When you run post plays, are they suppose to catch on the block or the 3pt line? Let's hear it Mr social media coach, Gm and President? You have no f***ing clue what we dealing with.

"Maybe you should ask the whole team individually how they feel on a serious note and then … rethink alot of s***."

Before that, Murray engaged with an NBACentral X post that noted how the Pelicans are 3-0 without him this season.

In a quote post, Murray used a slew of crying laughing emojis and then said this, as captured in a screenshot by a social media user:

"From what's going on INSIDE This sounds like someone hit you to say this!! THE 'SABOTAGE' IS REAL!!!!!!"

On Friday, he apparently reposted Charania's report about him wanting out of New Orleans. That repost no longer appears on his X feed, however.

Charania went on "NBA Today" Friday after breaking the news to flesh it out more:

"In the last several days, I'm told, Murray has met with the organization, has made it clear to them that he wants to go somewhere else and play a meaningful, key role on another team," Charania said on the program.

"And we've seen Dejounte Murray, especially on social media, express his frustration with how things are going there. Clearly, it is not working out there. He is not going to be playing basketball in New Orleans for the time moving forward here."

Charania noted that in Murray's absence, the Pelicans will turn over the lead guard position to 2025 No. 7 overall pick Jeremiah Fears. The 20-year-old Oklahoma product has averaged 18 points and nine assists in the three games Murray has missed this season.

Murray's been available for only 54 Pelicans games since he came aboard ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. He suffered a torn Achilles that season, and that injury kept him out of a good portion of last season, too.

Murray's best NBA season occurred in 2021-22, when he earned his All-Star recognition and led the league in steals during his final go-around with the San Antonio Spurs. He also spent two seasons with the Atlanta Hawks. They ultimately traded him to the Pelicans for two first-round picks, Dyson Daniels, Larry Nance Jr., E.J. Liddell and Cody Zeller.

#2710. James Harden is foundational to the Cavs’ Success

James Harden arrived to the Cleveland Cavaliers as a divisive figure.

As the centerpiece of a trade that sent fan favorite Darius Garland to the Clippers, Harden was always going to face an uphill battle.

Now, coming off an Eastern Conference Finals appearance, all eyes are on Harden as he begins his second season with the team. After twelve games, one thing is clear: his performance will determine whether the Cavaliers can improve on last year.

The vibes around Harden hit a low point after Cleveland was walloped by the Charlotte Hornets, 124-112, on November 9.

He was at the center of the team's problems. There were long stretches of minimal effort on defense, and he often looked like he was coasting, barely attempting to bring down rebounds.

Offensively, it was just as bleak: 11 points on 3-9 shooting with four turnovers. Safe to say, the fanbase was ready to drive Harden to the airport and send him to whatever team, or country, would take him.

Then came the Knicks game on November 11.

Suddenly, Harden was energized and putting his mark on the game.

He orchestrated a 115-107 road win at Madison Square Garden and put the offense on his back with 32 points, going 9-for-14 from the field with five threes and 9-11 at the free throw line.

Putting those two games back to back is as stark as it is telling of where the Cavaliers are. The team knew the risks and still entered the James Harden business.

This isn't MVP Harden, and this isn't the Houston Rockets of the 2010s, but the sentiment still stands: Cleveland is reliant on Harden to make the pieces on this roster gel. When he is at his worst, the ripples spread throughout the entire lineup.

The numbers show just how much his play matters, if not in the way Cleveland hoped. Through his first 11 games, the Cavaliers had a -5.6 net rating with Harden on the floor and a +15.7 net rating with him off it. Whatever his Knicks performance does to those numbers, it was a long way from enough to erase them.

Is this too much to ask of a 37-year-old? Yes. But the Cavaliers knew this was the route they were taking when they traded for Harden and then extended him on a three-year, $97 million deal. At times this season, it has looked like a grave mistake.

Harden is posting some of the lowest numbers of his career: 16.7 points, 5.6 assists and 4.6 rebounds per game. That scoring is about seven points below his 23.6 average last season, and about four below the 20.5 he averaged in 26 games after joining Cleveland. His assists are down more than two per game from last season's 8.0.

Still, the Knicks game suggests the player fans expect isn't gone. The problem for the Cavaliers is how to keep Harden engaged and empowered enough that performances like that don't become few and far between.

It will be a balancing act. Cleveland has to meet Harden at a level of comfort that lets him use his best traits, while melding his heliocentric style with an offense that fits the rest of the roster and lets the ball move more freely. That will take time. The Cavaliers knew this came with Harden, and fans need to understand it won't be pretty until a resolution is found on the court.

#2705. The Goal of the Utah Jazz This Season: Win The NBA Cup

If you follow me on TikTok or Twitter you may already know this about me, but for those who don't: I am a BIG NBA Cup supporter. We #RespectTheCup in this house. I am also a big soccer (or as I call it, footy) fan, so I was already prone to enjoying these in-season tournaments. When it was announced I actually think that I was one of the only ones in my content creation circle, and certainly the only one in my friend group, to be 100% on board with the idea.

While Adam Silver has had more missteps in the last few years than I would prefer, he knocked it out of the park with the NBA Cup. As mentioned above, I think that there are ways to improve the tournament, but even in its short existence, it has brought much needed excitement and punch to the early portion of the NBA season.

The Utah Jazz haven't had the season that any of us would have envisioned, and while starting 1-11 is quite the hole to put ourselves in, the NBA Cup allows us to strive towards a real goal outside of "development." Even more important than presenting an opportunity to lift up some hardware, getting all the way to the NBA Cup Final would prove that this team is ready to compete one day.

The NBA Cup's lineage is relatively short, but in its brief history we've been able to see some truly great basketball teams compete for the prize. If we take a trip down memory lane, we will notice something almost immediately — the teams that make it are/were threats to the rest of the league.

These weren't flukes, they were mistakes; if you made it to the Final, you were a team with the aspirations and the roster to play basketball in June.

The inaugural NBA Cup Final was a success by every single metric there is. The game drew 4.58 million viewers between ABC and ESPN, the arena in Las Vegas hosted over 19,000 fans, and the Final featured one of the most exciting teams in the league at the time in the Indiana Pacers and the one of the most well known brands in all of sports in the Los Angeles Lakers, of course led by LeBron James – one of the most recognizable athletes in the world.

While the Lakers weren't world beaters at this time, being three years removed from a championship, the year prior this squad lost in the Western Conference Finals to the ever dangerous Denver Nuggets. On the other side of the bracket, Tyrese Haliburton and the Indiana Pacers were the talk of the town. Haliburton was coming off of an All-Star campaign the year prior and the Pacers were just so fun to watch. The matchup also presented an opportunity for there to be a "passing of the torch" moment, but LeBron had other plans.

LeBron finished the game with 24 points, 11 rebounds, and 4 assists, Anthony Davis had a game of a lifetime with 41 points and 20 rebounds, and Austin Reaves chipped in 28 points off the bench in route to a 123-109 victory. LeBron won the inaugural NBA Cup MVP award, the most recognizable NBA team in the world won the inaugural NBA Cup, and the win reiterated that the Los Angeles Lakers were still going to compete at the highest level.

While I was personally rooting for the Indiana Pacers in this game, they gave it everything they had. Haliburton had a cool 20 point and 11 assist performance while Bennedict Mathurin scored 20 off the bench. It wasn't the result that they (or I) wanted, but it wasn't long before they proved to be worthy opponents themselves. Lest we forget that the Pacers could have been one catastrophic injury away from lifting up the Larry O'Brien Trophy the following year in the 2024-2025 NBA Season.

The second iteration of the NBA Cup had quite the shoes to fill, but the NBA Cup Final did not disappoint. While there wasn't a widely recognizable brand in the Final like the Lakers or the Celtics, there was a massive amount of star power.

The Milwaukee Bucks were just a few years removed from a NBA Championship themselves, and Giannis Antetokounmpo was out to prove that they could still compete. Giannis was, and still is, one of the the world's best players and one of the game's biggest names. With Damian Lillard at his side, Giannis was out to prove that the Bucks were still threats to come out of the East.

Over in the West, the Oklahoma City Thunder were taking the league by storm. The year prior the team showed up on everyone's radar after winning 57 games, and this year turned out to be no different. After it was all said and done, the OKC Thunder won 68 games led by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander who won his first MVP award, and the crew hoisted the Larry O'Brien Trophy at the end of the year.

Unfortunately for the Thunder, Giannis and the Bucks weren't ready to lose this night. Giannis lead the way with a 26 point, 19 rebound, and 10 assist triple-double while Damian Lillard scored 23 points and led the Bucks to a 97-81 victory.

The Power of Friendship didn't help the Thunder on this night, but they did give it their best effort: SGA scored 21, Jalen Williams scored 18,and Isaiah Hartenstein chipped in 16. While they weren't victorious this night, they did prove to the world that they could compete with anyone in the league. After making it all the way to the NBA Cup Final, they dominated the regular season and defeated the aforementioned Indiana Pacers in 7 games in the NBA Finals.

The third iteration of the NBA Cup was arguably the best of the three. It also combined the best of both worlds from the previous two matchups: mega star power AND a recognizable brand. The New York Knicks are either the second or third (depending on who you ask) most recognizable brand in all of basketball, and for good reason. They don't call Madison Square Garden "The Mecca of Basketball" for no reason. To top it all off, the Knicks were coming off of a 51 win season and a Conference Finals appearance the previous year, and Jalen Brunson just made the All-NBA 2nd Team.

Out west the San Antonio Spurs were well ahead of schedule with their roster. Stephon Castle just won the Rookie of the Year award the previous year, they drafted Dylan Harper with the #2 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, and Victor Wembanyama had displayed All-World potential despite missing most of the 2024-2025 NBA season with DVT. To a lesser extent compared to the Knicks, the Spurs are also a world wide brand in the basketball realm due to the success of international stars like Tony Parker and Manu Ginobili.

With all of the star power and recognizable brands at play, it shouldn't be a surprise that the Amazon Prime Video broadcast averaged over 3 million viewers. What also wasn't a surprise is that both teams came to play. The Spurs had 7 players in double figures; Wemby and Dylan Harper combined for 39 points off the bench, while Stephon Castle scored 15 points and dropped 12 dimes as a starter. For the Knicks, their Power of Friendship mantra rang true with 7 players scoring in double digits led by Jalen Brunson's 25 points and OG Anunoby's 28 points.

The Knicks came out on top 124-113, but this was just the appetizer for the NBA Finals. In the NBA Cup Final both teams proved that they had what it took to compete at the highest level, and then they both powered their way through the NBA Playoffs to meet in the NBA Finals. Unfortunately for The Baseline Bums, the Knicks prevailed again in a 4-1 series win to secure a championship for the first time in 53 years.

Time and time again, the NBA Cup has proven to be the battleground for future competitors and NBA Championship threats. In all three years of existence, the teams competing in the NBA Cup have either already climbed to the mountain top or they were getting ready to take the league by storm. THAT is what we should be striving for. I think after the 1-11 start it would be very difficult to compete for a Playoff spot (I predicted that we would finish 7th) so we should strive to do something more enticing than another year of developing our young talent.

We had higher expectations for our team, but we've had a season from hell when it comes to the injury department: Jaren Jackson Jr. is out until the new year, Jusuf Nurkic will be out for at least another two weeks, and Lauri Markkanen will miss at least a month with his hand fracture. Do I think that it will be difficult to win the games necessary to advance in the NBA Cup tournament without them? Absolutely. Do I think that this is a tremendous chance for our young players to prove what they can do? Without a doubt.

The road will be hard, especially after dropping our first NBA Cup game against the Mavericks 112-100, but I don't think that our chance to win has been snuffed out. Tonight we play the Houston Rockets, and while they are formidable, they are not unbeatable. After that, the Suns and Nuggets are both very volatile. There is a real scenario where the Jazz go 3-1 in group play and earn a spot in the NBA Cup Quarter Finals. Once we get there, it just takes a hot streak to take us all the way to the Promised Land.

Again, without Lauri or JJJ, the burden will be placed on our younger players and luckily we have the firepower to do it. Keyonte George is good for 20 points a game this year, Darryn Peterson became the first teenager in Utah Jazz history to score 20+ points in four straight games, and Ace Bailey has proven that he is invaluable to this team.

The season has been disappointing so far, but there are reasons to be excited and goals to strive for. There is a lot of basketball left to play this year, and I for one am not satisfied with chalking up this year to another development year. Our goal for the rest of the year should be to win the NBA Cup, because if we can do that with a depleted roster, just imagine what we can do in the 2027-2028 season with a fully heathy squad.

How do you feel about the NBA Cup? How do you think the Jazz will fare the rest of the season? Sound off in the comments below!

#2700. Dejounte Murray’s trade request creates an opportunity for the Suns

Over the first eleven games of the season, it has not all been sunshine and rainbows for this Suns team. They have seen injuries, rebounding issues, and lapses on both ends of the floor. This has brought them to a 5-6 record, which lets them beat the bad teams but struggle against the good ones. As Espo from PHNX said the other night, they are basically in basketball purgatory right now, and some things need to change. Regardless of whether it's a lineup switch, plugging in Jordan Goodwin or Collin Gillespie for Jalen Green, or potentially a trade on the horizon.

In last night's contest against the Charlotte Hornets, we saw Jalen Green benched and not finish the game. This move allowed the Suns to regain their lead and still win a game they should have controlled the whole way. Since Green hasn't been playing well in the lineup and has been forced into this playmaking role, many are making him the scapegoat for the team's early-season struggles.

While they are right to put most of the blame on him, it is not entirely his fault, as sometimes the bigs have trouble rebounding or some of the forwards are not locked in defensively.

This is where Green has become a devalued asset across the league, as they now know he cannot fit with this starting lineup, and the Suns will likely switch things up as we get closer to the deadline. With Green still 24, some lottery teams will likely be willing to take a chance on him and let him shine with their club. For the Suns, today's news may have made that landing spot clearer.

Dejounte Murray of the New Orleans Pelicans has requested a trade. I've highlighted him multiple times as a good target for the Suns for many reasons, but now that his value is depleted and he's on the market, this is the perfect trade for both teams. Both teams have an asset with depreciated value that could help the other franchise, and everyone seems to be catching on.

They've also been linked to Murray via Chris Haynes in this tweet. Haynes was the first to address locker-room concerns via the Suns, saying many felt the team needed a true point guard. Well, Murray could come in and fill that role as a better fit for the starters, but also mesh into the defensive identity that Jordan Ott wants to bring to this Phoenix team,

Murray, who has a $30.8 million player option next season, would accept it heading into next offseason but at 30, doesn't seem to want a long-term, expensive deal. On the other hand, Green is young and looking to extend long term. With Booker's contract coming up, plus the Brooks extension and a potential Bridges extension, and Beal's dead money, it doesn't seem feasible to pay all four players, especially when they look this bad on the court together.

Green is also the same player option as Murray, just at $36 million, and is making that same amount this season, so not only would you save $4 million this season and $6 million next year, but you would save yourself from a pain-inducing contract negotiation. It is clear Green can't be a starter given his recent play, and Murray, who has been a head case in NOLA, may be the same, but it's an unknown.

I feel Murray, who has been frustrated with the Pelicans this season, will buy into the Suns' culture once he gets here. As we know, the Pelicans are bad and lack a clear direction for building. They view Herb Jones and Trey Murphy III as high pieces but not the building blocks of their rebuild. It seems like there are three timelines: Jones and Murphy III, Zion Williamson, and Murray as the vets who can help with a playoff push, and then you've got Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen as the young building blocks. Getting a young player like Green may not be the best fit, but it would give him a chance to return to his scoring form and try to become their number-one offensive option.

For the Suns, this move frees up some money and gives you a player who can hopefully buy into the culture and help alleviate some of the pain for your best player. Murray isn't coming in as a game-changing secondary option, but if he can buy into the team role and do the little things, he could find some great success in this starting lineup. Murray was an all-caliber defender in San Antonio, and yeah, he's had many injuries, but I still think some of that player is still in him if he gets to Phoenix.

Ultimately, time will tell whether the Suns make this move or switch their starting lineups first. One good thing to know, though, is that Murray wants out, and the Suns look like one of the only teams that would need a true point guard. With both Green and Murray at their lowest values and on similar contracts, it seems a one-for-one deal could be the easiest thing for both parties. That said, the Pelicans front office doesn't have the best track record with trades, so maybe the Suns can get something else thrown in for taking on their disgruntled player, since Green hasn't made his frustrations as obvious as Murray's. Could the Suns try to get a pick back in exchange for a younger asset? That's something I'd like to see them try to pull off, alongside bringing in Murray to give them more flexibility in the long term.

What are your thoughts? Is Dejounte Murray someone you would like the Suns to go after? Is there another piece you think would be a better fit? Ultimately, given what assets the Suns have to trade, this may be the best option they can pursue without hurting their depth too much, and I'd like it to materialize.

#2699. Nationwide ground stop potentially complicates NFL, college games

The sudden nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA will potentially impact this weekend’s football games.

It’s only the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11. It’s apparently due to a widespread outage impacting air-traffic control functions.

Visiting NFL teams typically travel to the sites of their games on Saturday; if the situation lingers, some teams may not be able to get to where they need to be. More immediately, college teams that travel on Friday have a mess.

As noted by Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area, the 49ers usually travel on Friday for games that are at least two time zones away. For Sunday’s game against the Cowboys, they plan to travel on Saturday.

Some teams can get to the locations of their games by car or train. The distance from Minneapolis to Green Bay is 279 miles. For Buffalo to New Jersey (for Bills-Jets), it’s also less than 300 miles.

It’s roughly 290 miles fom Pittsburgh to Cincinnati, and 373 miles from L.A. to Phoenix.

For the other games (particularly Chargers-Ravens on Monday night), it’s a long way to go via ground transportation.

#2698. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2696. John Harbaugh: Cam Skattebo was not supposed to push on Jameis Winston sneak

Giants coach John Harbaugh defended running back Cam Skattebo, who stayed in his stance on a crucial Jameis Winston quarterback sneak during Thursday night’s loss to the Commanders.

Harbaugh said the call was a quarterback sneak but not a tush push, and Skattebo wasn’t supposed to be pushing Winston.

“We had a certain check involved in it, so he wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing. We didn’t call the same [QB sneak] that we’ve been calling,” Harbaugh said, via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News. “What else am I supposed to say? He wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing.”

Why the Giants wouldn’t want Skattebo to push Winston in an attempt to get the first down yardage is unclear, but the play looked strange, and it was a big one for the Giants, who had a 21-17 lead late in the fourth quarter at the time, but couldn’t hold the lead after getting stuffed on that quarterback sneak and lost 24-21.

Reaves left Wednesday's win over Milwaukee in the third quarter and didn't return. Quentin Grimes, who missed two games because of a sprained finger on his right hand, participated in the live portion of the stay-ready game against coaches Wednesday and said he expects to play Sunday. Grimes wore tape on his right pinky finger while speaking with reporters.

"I had a really good day just playing with a little wrap over it," Grimes said. "Just seeing how it felt the first time, but it felt really good. We got a lot of wins out there in them games, at least. But it felt really good out there."

#2687. Braves Lock Up Evan Phillips For Bullpen Depth

The Atlanta Braves just wrote another check for relief pitching, and they did not blink. Evan Phillips is coming to town after the team paid a premium price to secure his arm. The signing of Evan Phillips shocks no one who has watched the front office spend big on late-inning arms in recent years. According to Battery Power, the signing came out of nowhere, arriving as a bolt from the blue for fans who expected rotation help instead.

Atlanta needed a fix because Raisel Iglesias is still a free agent with no guarantee of a return. The club cannot rely on hope when it comes to closing games. They need proven arms that can handle the pressure of the eighth and ninth innings. Battery Power notes that if Iglesias does return, it will likely be on a one-year deal, leaving the team to add even more talent to the mix. The team must build a bullpen that can dominate late in games.

Everyone asked if Phillips could stay on the mound after missing most of 2025 and 2026 with injuries. The answer is yes, and the numbers prove his stuff is back to elite levels. With a 97 mph fastball in 2026, he ranked in the 85th percentile for velocity among all pitchers. Battery Power reports he also posted a 31.1 percent strikeout rate while keeping his walk rate down to just 5.7 percent.

His secondary pitches show the same dominance that made him a star before his Tommy John surgery. His sweeper sat at 86 mph, three miles per hour above the average for right-handers. The cutter hit 93 mph, also three miles above average, while his sinker reached 97 mph. These are not just good numbers; they are the marks of a pitcher who can shut down opposing lineups.

Braves fans should feel good about the shape of the bullpen heading into the 2027 season. Dylan Lee and Robert Suarez already anchor the high-leverage spots, and now Phillips joins that group. The team might still bring back Iglesias to form a one-two punch, but the depth is already there.

Relievers are volatile and injuries happen, but the talent level is undeniable. The front office is not playing it safe with a cheap option; they are buying the best available talent on the market. This approach mirrors the aggressive spending that has defined the franchise's recent success. The Braves are set to field a dangerous bullpen if the arms stay healthy.

#2686. Vikings name Week 10 starter vs Packers after Kirk Cousins trade

The Minnesota Vikings finally made the announcement that many have been expecting for several days.

Quarterback Kirk Cousins will start against the Green Bay Packers in Week 10, head coach Kevin O'Connell announced on Friday, Nov. 13. The intra-divisional game will mark the start of Cousins' second stint in Minnesota, three years after his last game for the Vikings.

"Kirk Cousins will start the football game. Cannot give him enough credit for coming in here, how he's gone about the week. Both him and the coaching staff getting him ready to go, working extremely hard, using all the time we possibly can," O'Connell said.

"It's been really impressive, what he's been able to do ... just getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with, but certainly some guys he hasn't. It's been something that everybody's been very, very impressed by. Excited to start Kirk in the game, see him play on Sunday."

KIRK COUSINS: Veteran QB kept mum about his chance to start Week 10

Coincidentally, the upcoming Nov. 15 clash will be Cousins' second straight matchup against the Packers as the Vikings' starting quarterback. The last game the 38-year-old played for Minnesota, in 2023, was also at Lambeau Field.

Cousins' first stint with the Vikings ended unceremoniously – trainers had to cart him off of the field after he tore his Achilles during a game his team went on to win. In the offseason that followed, the Vikings allowed him to walk in free agency, and he went on to sign a four-year, $180 million contract with the Atlanta Falcons.

Cousins said in his (re-)introductory press conference with the Vikings on Nov. 11 that he expects the Week 10 game to be meaningful. It's both his first game back with Minnesota but also his return to Lambeau Field for the first time since the 2023 injury.

"It means a lot to play at Lambeau Field, no matter what the circumstances," Cousins said. "Knowing that that was where I was carted off, and I had thoughts of, 'Is this my last game? Is this my last game as a Viking?' To be back out there, wearing the purple and gold. It has meaning, but you have to go make it mean something with the way you play."

In nine starts with the Las Vegas Raiders this season, Cousins has a 4-5 record. He was 202-of-315 passing for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. His 97.1 passer rating so far this season is his highest since his previous stint with Minnesota.

The Vikings are hoping the addition of Cousins will help kick-start an offensive resurgence. The team has lost two straight following a 6-0 start, and it sits in third place in a tightly contested NFC North.

While the defense has been a strong point – the 14.5 points per game the unit has allowed so far is the fewest in the league – the offense has struggled. Minnesota's 18.3 points scored per game are sixth-fewest in the NFL.

#2684. A sudden FAA ground stop strands teams and throws the sports weekend into chaos

The Federal Aviation Administration's decision to ground all flights nationwide Friday threw the sports world into chaos, leaving NBA, NHL and college teams stranded as they tried to reach their destinations, and NFL teams were left to wonder whether the issue would be resolved in time for them to travel to their games this weekend.

The FAA issued a notice that said the ground stop was "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy later said there was a communications issue affecting the 22 regional air traffic control centers that direct planes en route between airports nationwide, and that FAA technicians were investigating.

"There's no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they're flying," Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said.

Most college football teams playing Saturday travel the day before their game, and the stoppage left many schools — including No. 2 Utah, eighth-ranked Texas and No. 9 Tennessee — at a standstill as they departed for road games. The Utes play at No. 22 Arizona, the Longhorns visit No. 24 LSU and the Vols are traveling to Texas A&M in three of the bigger games of the weekend.

In the case of the Longhorns, they posted on social media a short video of them boarding their plane before the stoppage. If they end up taking a bus to Baton Rouge, the trip for the 6:30 p.m. CT kickoff Saturday takes about seven hours.

"We are grounded and waiting to see when we can leave," a team spokesman said.

Other schools affected by the stoppage included No. 19 Ole Miss, Baylor, Kansas State, Washington and Minnesota.

It also was unclear whether referees, who typically fly to their assignments the day before games, would make it on time.

Several teams were able to take off before the stoppage went into effect, including Missouri, which was flying to No. 1 Georgia; Duke, which was traveling to No. 5 Miami; and No. 10 Texas Tech, which was on the way to Oklahoma State.

Meanwhile, the Nets were among five NBA teams scheduled to fly Friday for games on Saturday. They had just boarded the team plane in New Orleans after playing the Pelicans earlier this week when their flight to Memphis was halted in place.

The Pistons flew earlier in the day to Miami. The Cavaliers, Bulls and Grizzlies play Friday night and were due to fly afterward.

There are 14 scheduled games in the NHL on Saturday. And while the Panthers made it to St. Louis for their game before the stoppage began, the Sharks were among those that were left waiting to leave for their game in Utah.

The FAA did not provide a timeline for restarting flights, leaving sporting events taking place beyond Saturday in limbo. That includes most of the Week 10 schedule in the NFL along with numerous college sporting events.

AP Sports Writers Jim Vertuno, Aaron Beard and Tim Reynolds contributed to this report.

#2682. Chiefs-Falcons Madden Simulation Week 10: On the Road Again

On Sunday, the (6-2) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road again taking on the (3-6) Atlanta Falcons. Let's see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 27.

Note: Madden simulation is 7-1 this season, predicting the outcome.

If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can't see it, click here.

The Falcons' opening drive gained just seven yards before they were forced to punt on their first possession.

The Chiefs' ground-and-pound attack erupted on their first drive, highlighted by a 28-yard run from Kenneth Walker. Walker rushed for 36 yards on the drive, while backup running back Emmett Johnson added 13 yards on a third-and-10 run to move the chains.

The drive would end with Harrison Butker drilling a 44-yard field goal to open the scoring.

End of first quarter: Chiefs 3, Falcons 0

The Falcons opened the quarter at the Chiefs' 19-yard line. Drake London caught a 15-yard pass to reach the four-yard line. From the pistol formation, Michael Penix Jr. handed the ball to Bijan Robinson, who ran to the right, broke a tackle, and found the end zone for a touchdown.

The Chiefs failed to reach the first-down marker on their next possession and were forced to punt the ball back to Atlanta.

A 14-yard pick-and-roll pass to Jahan Dotson moved the ball to the Chiefs' 14-yard line. Bijan Robinson finished the drive by catching a pass from Penix Jr. and scoring his second touchdown of the game.

The Chiefs found themselves at midfield with a minute remaining in the quarter. On third-and-three, Rashee Rice ran a comeback route and picked up the first down to keep the drive alive. Mahomes then connected with newly acquired Josh Downs for a 12-yard gain and another first down.

The Chiefs managed to put points on the board before halftime as Butker drilled his second field goal of the game, this time from 44 yards out, cutting the Falcons' lead to eight.

End of second quarter: Falcons 14, Chiefs 6

Josh Downs hauled in an 18-yard pass on a deep out route, going up to make the catch while keeping both feet in bounds. The reception moved the Chiefs to the Falcons' 25-yard line.

Two plays later, Xavier Watts intercepted Mahomes on a high throw intended for Rashee Rice running a crossing route.

The Falcons turned to their running game to drain the clock, alternating between Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson.

Another 11-yard run from Bijan Robinson moved Atlanta to the Chiefs' 11-yard line. Brina Robinson followed it up with a 10-yard run to carry the Falcons into the fourth quarter.

End of third quarter: Falcons 14, Chiefs 6

A toss to Bijan Robinson went untouched into the end zone for his third touchdown of the game, extending Atlanta's lead.

The Chiefs found themselves at their own 48-yard line facing a third-and-five. From the shotgun, Mahomes delivered a strike on a fly route to Jalen Royals, who hauled in the pass for a touchdown to bring the game back within one score.

The Falcons reached midfield on their next possession but were stopped at the Chiefs' 48-yard line and forced to punt.

Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce for 16 yards to move the Chiefs to their own 48-yard line.

Downs followed with a 26-yard reception on an out route.

Royals then hauled in a 17-yard pass on a deep crossing route to move the Chiefs to the nine-yard line.

Mahomes went back to the player who helped get the drive started. Kelce was targeted inside the red zone and came down with the touchdown to bring Kansas City closer.

The Chiefs attempted a two-point conversion to tie the game, but the Falcons stopped a screen pass intended for Johnson.

Kansas City's defense came up with a three-and-out on the Falcons' next possession, giving the Chiefs another opportunity. Atlanta was forced to punt, leaving Kansas City with one timeout and eight seconds remaining before the two-minute warning.

The Chiefs crossed midfield after Mahomes connected with Kelce for a 14-yard gain. However, the next play went backward as Mahomes was sacked for an eight-yard loss.

The sack put Kansas City in a fourth-and-13 situation with 15 seconds remaining.

The Chiefs' final attempt fell incomplete as Mahomes tried to make a throw while being taken down by the pass rush. Kansas City turned the ball over on downs, ending its comeback attempt.

Patrick Mahomes: 29 for 39 passing, 293 yards, 2 touchdowns, 1 interception, 1 rushing attempt, 7 yards

Kenneth Walker: 4 rushing attempts, 40 yards

Travis Kelce: 7 receptions, 74 yards, 1 touchdown.

Jalen Royals: 6 receptions, 82 yards. 1 touchdown

Harrison Butker: 2 for 2, long of 44 yards.

Michael Penix Jr.: 16 for 22 passing, 171 yards, 1 touchdown, 4 rushing attempts, 16 yards.

Bijan Robinson: 16 rushing attempts, 100 yards, 2 touchdowns

#2679. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick provided an injury update on shooting guard Austin Reaves.

Redick stated during his Friday, Nov. 13 media availability that Reaves suffered a bruised heel and is considered day-to-day. The coach added that Reaves and the team's medical staff opted against having imaging done on the injury.

Reaves had landed awkwardly on his left heel after missing a transition dunk attempt in the middle of the third quarter of the Lakers' 123-112 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Nov. 11.

After feeling some discomfort, he limped back to the locker room. The initial X-rays taken at the arena were negative, and Redick ruled out any potential Achilles tendon damage.

Dončić: Lakers star 'feeling good' after injury scare

Reaves and the Lakers will have more time to rest before traveling to Phoenix to take on the Suns at 4 p.m. ET (2 p.m. local) on Sunday, Nov. 15.

#2677. Buffalo Bills safety Amani Hooker will make his debut Week 10 vs. NY Jets

It took all of three practices for Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady to decide that Amani Hooker, the team's new addition at safety, will play in Week 10 against the New York Jets. In meeting with members of the media, Brady revealed that Hooker "definitely is gonna play, and excited to see whatever that role kind of looks like."

The Bills and president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane knew the time was right to take advantage of the looming trade deadline. In doing so, Buffalo has brought in someone they immediately identified as a starter for defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's system.

Brady, ever the master press chess player, was careful not to reveal too much about their plans for Hooker. He did say that play time is yet to be determined, noting that "from a comfort level, we don't want to put him out there and do anything that is not fair to him and the team." Brady and the team's defensive coaches have been impressed with Hooker's ability to quickly assimilate within the team's defense, including the ability to "communicate in our language."

Hooker's arrival means that once again veteran safety Damar Hamlin is likely to take a step back into a reserve role. Despite that, Hamlin has embraced his new teammate, helping him get comfortable with his new role in Buffalo.

Brady was asked about Hamlin and he emphatically stated that "Damar Hamlin has an incredibly important role on this football team, and he's gonna play a big part on this football team in a lot of different areas."He did acknowledge that Hooker's arrival might prove frustrating for Hamlin, who seemed to play well the last two games, and spoke about the situation at length, saying:

"Look, regardless of (if) someone says it or not, anytime you have an opportunity to be a starter and then you trade for somebody else, it can be a natural tendency to kind of maybe get frustrated. Right? But I believe Damar, and the safeties, and the team — we have a lot of guys on this team that can put pride aside and say 'hey whatever we gotta do to win a football game'… …that's what Damar Hamlin's all about and that's what he's always been about. He just wants opportunities to compete, and he's out there competing. And if it helps the Buffalo Bills, that's what he's about. So, that's why we love him and that's why — the trade was not an indication of Damar Hamlin, and more so just an opportunity for us to improve our football team."

Though Hooker will, in fact, make his Bills debut in Week 10, it's possible we still see Hamlin in action on defense depending on the situation. He may also reclaim a significant role on special teams, where the last two games Hamlin played zero snaps with the special teams units.
